title: Azure Account and Environment Setup
description: Create an Azure account, install the Azure CLI, and configure Visual Studio for Azure development.

data.text: Before calling Azure from C#, you need an Azure subscription, the Azure CLI, and the right workload in Visual Studio or the .NET CLI.

data.title: Account setup steps
items: Go to https://azure.microsoft.com/free and click **Start free**
Sign in with a Microsoft account or GitHub account
Verify your identity with a phone number and credit card
You get $200 credit for 30 days plus limited free services for 12 months

data.title: Credit card required
data.text: Azure free accounts require a credit card for identity verification, but many popular services stay free for 12 months and others stay always free.
The Azure CLI works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It lets you script Azure operations from PowerShell, Bash, or C# processes.

data.title: Install Azure CLI on Windows with winget
data.content: Use winget to install the Azure CLI.

data.title: Verify installation and log in
data.content: After installation, open a new terminal and run these commands.

items: In Visual Studio Installer, select the **Azure development** workload
In `dotnet new`, install templates with `dotnet workload install microsoft-web` if needed
The Azure SDK for .NET comes through NuGet packages per service

data.title: Create your first resource group
data.description: A resource group is a logical container for Azure resources.
steps: Run `az login` and complete the browser login
Run `az account show` to confirm your subscription
data.expectedOutcome: You see a JSON response with `provisioningState: Succeeded` and the new resource group name.

data.title: Environment Checklist
points: Azure free account created with verified identity
Azure CLI installed and `az login` succeeds
Visual Studio has the Azure development workload or .NET CLI is ready
One resource group created for the exercises in this course
data.takeaway: With an account, CLI, and resource group, you are ready to provision Azure resources from the command line and from C#.
